question: Should OpenClaw accept a WhatsApp-specific `channels.whatsapp.progressMessages` config surface for sparse text progress, or should WhatsApp rely on existing lifecycle reactions/block streaming until a shared channel progress API exists?
rationale: This PR adds a new user-facing config option and message cadence behavior, and repository policy treats config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive product choices even when disabled by default.

options.title: Accept After Repairs And Proof
options.body: Keep the opt-in surface only after the blocking code issues are fixed, real WhatsApp proof is added, and the config contract is complete.

options.title: Defer To Existing Status Surfaces
options.body: Close or pause this direction and continue using lifecycle status reactions/block streaming for WhatsApp progress until stronger user demand appears.

options.title: Require A Shared Progress API First
options.body: Ask for a smaller core/plugin API design so WhatsApp, Signal, and other non-editing channels can share one progress-message contract.

recommendation.title: Accept After Repairs And Proof
recommendation.body: Keep the opt-in surface only after the blocking code issues are fixed, real WhatsApp proof is added, and the config contract is complete.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the listed maintainer and has recent WhatsApp config/docs history, making him the best available product-direction owner for a new public config surface.
